data.turoyo: Koḥoze: nafəqle ʕaṣro, ḥamšaḥsar=rawixe, i=nuro kqədḥo me femayye. Kulle b rəmḥe, b sayfe.
data.translation: Da sieht er: es kommen zehn, fünfzehn Reiter auf ihn zu, denen das Feuer aus dem Munde flammt, alle mit Lanzen und Schwerten.

rationale: Thin Infectum I.1 cell; feminine fire subject and explicit source me femayye add a different form and concrete flame-emission context.

summary: All nine full occurrences were reviewed. Most are exact inherited quotations; only the fire-from-mouths context is added.
I.1 is intransitive flaming/burning, I.2 is agentive ignition/fire-striking, and I.3 is the specifically established anger image. A fiery admiring gaze does not entail anger.

Intransitive subjects include lightning, fire and a lamp; me femayye supplies a source. The feather is an unmarked patient of Preterit I.2, whereas the demon can be expressed with the L-series agent after qdəḥle.

Part act. qaḏiḥto with -wa expresses a long-standing lamp state; Infectum-wa in 69/311 expresses habitual fire-making. No Preterit Intransitive occurrence is established by these records, so the inherited tentative empty box stays empty.

The source has d/ḏ variants, and the permitted qḏḥ lookup confirms a parallel separately filed family. The inherited qdḥ entry already notes majority ḏ pronunciation in II; do not merge roots or automatically move forms between II and III from orthography alone.

The reader's entry-wide Transitive objection mislocates the note: the supplied Transitive wording is under II. I.1 already has intransitive glosses and examples, so no unnecessary gloss rewrite is made.
No fixed idiom, light-verb addition, or new rubbing sense is supported. German rieb in the feather scene remains the edition's wording, not proof that qdḥ means rub.
At PrS 26/11 was the feather ignited to summon the horse, or is there independent evidence for a rubbing operation? The edition rieb alone cannot establish a new sense.
Reconcile inherited prs 63/9 and prs 157/18 with supplied PrS 26/11 and58/24 before counting the same contexts twice or replacing numbering systems.
How should the editors coordinate qdḥ and qḏḥ, especially qdḥ II versus qḏḥ III? These source variants do not justify a silent paradigm merger.
Does the tentative Preterit Intransitive box have independent evidence outside this assignment? None of the nine records supplies it.
